title: Formalized provability: reasoning about proofs inside arithmetic

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Express proof checking and consistency in arithmetic, and distinguish numerical proofs from the uniform derivability conditions.
abstract: If a formal system proves a sentence, can it also prove that a proof of that sentence exists? For an extension of Robinson arithmetic whose axioms can be listed by a program, an actual proof supplies exactly such a proof of provability. We then ask how much of this reasoning the system can carry out for arbitrary claimed proofs, rather than for one given finite proof. That change leads to the derivability conditions used in incompleteness arguments. Verifying individual numerical cases does not establish all these conditions. Keeping the proof predicate fixed makes clear what has been proved, what still needs an internal proof, and which arithmetic sentence expresses consistency.
